channel.title: Religion News Service - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Religion News Service (religionnews.com)

item.title: How one displaced family in Gaza is observing Ramadan’s first day under a fragile ceasefire deal
item.description: Ramadan arrived in Gaza under a fragile ceasefire deal, but many Palestinians there say the month's typically festive spirit is eluding them as they grapple with the hardships of their daily lives and the grief and losses of the war.

item.title: The travertine quarries that built ancient Rome are carving rock for a new generation of temples
item.description: Today, the same quarries that built Rome with their distinctive pock-marked travertine are still being dug out to build a new generation of churches, temples and mosques around the world — as well as banks, museums, government buildings and private homes.

item.title: Hegseth frames Trump policies as ‘biblical’ in address to Christian broadcasters
item.description: NASHVILLE, Tenn. (RNS) — During an address at the National Religious Broadcasters convention, the defense secretary told attendees that President Donald Trump is fighting for their faith and returning America to its Christian foundations.

item.title: Inspired by Catholic nuns, Kenyan Lutheran pastor becomes church’s first female presiding bishop
item.description: The Rev. Catherine Ngina Musau, a 55-year-old mother of two, was elected in November and will be installed in June.

item.title: John Paulk disavowed conversion therapy. Will his new podcast finally dismantle the ‘ex-gay’ myth?
item.description: Paulk was the poster child of the movement that promised to 'cure' people of homosexuality. His re-emergence is likely to trigger victims of the debunked practice.

item.title: Sacred marches and sacred music in a time of empire
item.description: Bad Bunny's joyful Super Bowl halftime show, a group of monks walking hundreds of miles for peace, protesters singing in the streets.

item.title: Cardinal Dolan says Vance apologized for claiming bishops were pro-immigrant for the money
item.description: Despite Dolan’s condemnation of Vance’s comments, he said in the EWTN interview that Vance is 'a very good guy. I enjoy him a lot.'

item.title: The grim satisfaction of AI doomsaying
item.description: Like depictions of the horrors of war may ennoble it, dire warnings about the AI future only make the technology seem inevitable.

item.title: At Brazil’s Carnival, the country’s religions fight for respect on a global stage
item.description: Carnival, a spectacle celebrating African deities and Catholic saints alike, has become a battleground for religious groups in Brazil.

item.title: Rev. James Martin On His Journey to Becoming a Priest, and the Catholic Church Today
item.description: Father Jim's new memoir, "Work in Progress", is full of hilarious stories, honest reflections, and the call to stand with the marginalized.
